extracted.intended_audience: writers (especially unagented authors) looking to participate in social-media pitch events to attract agents/editors or community feedback
extracted.subtask_description: A curated list of 2024 social-media (primarily Twitter) pitch events, each with who it’s for and how it runs; useful for writers preparing short manuscript pitches, opening lines, or queries to post using event-specific hashtags/platforms. Includes notes on platform changes, eligibility, and special rules for individual events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of pitch events
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitch events (pitch contests/parties) are usually one-day social-media events during which writers use a particular hashtag to get eyes on their manuscript pitches, often to attract agents and publishers or for community support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They typically require short, punchy pitches or specific formats (e.g., opening lines) and may be hosted on Twitter or moved to other platforms; treat this as the general operating model for all listed events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check organiser details before participating
rubrics_metrics.description: Event schedules, hashtags, and platforms frequently change, especially given uncertainty around Twitter; participants should double-check details on organisers’ social media or websites before taking part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is curated but may be updated—always confirm event dates, required hashtags, platform (Twitter, Bluesky, Threads, private sites), and any submission forms or practice periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: #QuestPit — hype event, manuscripts at all stages
rubrics_metrics.description: QuestPit is a hype/community event open to writers with manuscripts at all stages and may welcome industry participation (agents/editors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple QuestPit dates occur throughout the year; industry participation means agents/editors may interact—be professional and concise in pitches. Website and Twitter handles provided for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: #PBPitch — for unagented picture book writers (event-specific rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: PBPitch is aimed specifically at unagented picture book writers; the listing notes this event ran multiple times and that June 20, 2024 was its last run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the pbpitch website for submission instructions and whether the event continues; some events may end permanently (this one noted as ended after June 2024).

rubrics_metrics.name: #PopUpPit — separate hashtags for agent/editor attention
rubrics_metrics.description: PopUpPit is open to authors seeking representation (use #PopUpPitA) or attention from acquiring editors (use #PopUpPitE); also uses themed hashtag #LuckyPit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the correct suffix to target the right industry audience. PopUpPit was rebranded from a prior spontaneous trend—watch for rebrand-specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: #IWSGPit — event associated with Insecure Writer’s Support Group
rubrics_metrics.description: IWSGPit is linked to the Insecure Writer’s Support Group and follows their community rules and schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the IWSG site/Twitter account for specific posting instructions and any community norms around pitch formatting and interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: #ChaosPit — ‘describe your book badly’ community event
rubrics_metrics.description: ChaosPit is a just-for-fun, community-building pitch event in which you describe your book badly; intended as an author hype event though some agents have participated historically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tone is playful and intentionally offbeat; expect nontraditional, humorous pitches rather than formal query-style blurbs.

rubrics_metrics.name: #PitLight — authors-only positivity event; recruiting betas/CPs
rubrics_metrics.description: PitLight is an authors-only positivity event; participants can also look for beta readers and critique partners using hashtags #LookingForBetas and #LookingForCPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Event emphasizes supportive community engagement rather than industry-solicitation; follow authors-only rules and use the suggested hashtags if seeking readers/partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: #PitDark — for dark literature (horror, dark fantasy, crime)
rubrics_metrics.description: PitDark is aimed at writers of dark literature (examples: horror, dark fantasy, crime).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target your pitch to the genre expectations; check PitDark’s website/Twitter for any additional submission specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: #SEAsianPit — for self-identifying Southeast Asian writers/illustrators
rubrics_metrics.description: SEAsianPit is a hype event for self-identifying Southeast Asian writers and illustrators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Event centers representation—ensure you meet any self-identification guidance and check the event page for submission rules and platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: #KidLitPit — for unagented children’s authors (multiple mini-events)
rubrics_metrics.description: KidLitPit is for unagented children’s authors and runs multiple mini-events on Twitter across April and May.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the KidLitPit Twitter/website for specific mini-event dates, age ranges, and permitted submission formats (picture book, MG, YA breakdowns may apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: #JoyPit — for unagented feel-good fiction/nonfiction; moodboards encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: JoyPit is meant for unagented authors of ‘feel-good’ fiction and nonfiction; moodboards are encouraged as part of the pitch presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using moodboards, prepare visual assets and links per the event’s instructions; check the JoyPitch site for exact formatting guidance and hashtag use.

rubrics_metrics.name: #UnhingedPit — open to all; unconventional pitches encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: UnhingedPit is open to all writers and explicitly encourages unconventional pitches; traditional rules may not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a place to experiment with format and voice—expect and allow for very short, strange, or nonstandard pitch forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: #QueerPit — for 2SLGBTQIA+ writers; includes pre-event
rubrics_metrics.description: QueerPit is a social pitch event for 2SLGBTQIA+ writers; a pre-event (#PreQueerPit) exists shortly beforehand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the event’s community guidelines and use the pre-event to prepare or test pitches; check site/Twitter for submission mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: #PicantePit — for self-identifying Latinx/Latine adult and NA fiction authors
rubrics_metrics.description: PicantePit targets self-identifying Latinx/Latine writers of Adult and New Adult fiction; community Discord and openness to Latine authors noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Event infrastructure may include Discord; check whether pitches are posted on Twitter or hosted in community channels and follow inclusion guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: #SmallPitch — for unagented authors seeking small/indie presses; multi-platform
rubrics_metrics.description: SmallPitch helps unagented authors find homes at small/indie presses and takes place simultaneously on Twitter and Threads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare pitches suitable for indie acquisitions; monitor both platforms for differing rules or linked submission forms; see event website for detailed instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: #PitchDis — for unagented disabled writers; uses password-protected site
rubrics_metrics.description: PitchDis is for unagented disabled writers and is hosted on a password-protected section of their website for pitches; practice pitch form is available prior to event so participants can familiarise themselves with format. The community is migrating to Bluesky for social components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a controlled-access submission window; sign up for practice forms (available 5–9 August prior to the 10–12 Sept pitch dates) and follow instructions for receiving the password and posting. Check migration notes for platform changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: #LatinxPitch — Latinx kidlit writers/illustrators; shifted to website showcase with agent/editor review window
rubrics_metrics.description: LatinxPitch for Latinx kidlit writers/illustrators changed to a website showcase where pitches are submitted from 15–22 Sept and then viewed by agents/editors 23–27 Sept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This two-stage model separates submission and agent-review windows—prepare a pitch that reads well on a website showcase; follow submission window exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: #PitBLK — for Black writers; moved off Twitter to private pitch site with staged review
rubrics_metrics.description: PitBLK is for Black writers and has moved off Twitter to a private pitch site; pitch submissions occur during a submission window and agents/editors review later (submission 21–25 Sept; review 30 Sept–4 Oct noted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the private site’s submission rules and timing; understand that access is restricted to protect community members and to manage agent/editor interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: #1stLinePit — post your opening lines
rubrics_metrics.description: 1stLinePit asks authors to post opening lines; open to authors of all genres at all stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft a compelling opening line specifically—this event is judged by first-sentence impact rather than full-synopsis or query format.

rubrics_metrics.name: #KidLitGN — for middle-grade and younger graphic novels (agented or unagented)
rubrics_metrics.description: KidLitGN is for writers and illustrators of middle grade and younger graphic novels; hosts include its own website and social accounts; YA graphic novel pitches can be submitted to a sister site (YA GN Pitch).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the site’s submission format for GN pitches; note age category distinctions and sister-site options for YA GN.

rubrics_metrics.name: #SkyPitch — picture book pitches on Bluesky
rubrics_metrics.description: SkyPitch is for picture book authors and takes place exclusively on Bluesky.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you’re new to Bluesky, create an account and read the SkyPitch site for posting rules; platform-exclusive events require platform familiarity ahead of time.

rubrics_metrics.name: #SWANApit — for writers from South West Asia and North Africa with mentoring opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: SWANApit is for writers from South West Asia and North Africa; mentoring opportunities open in Fall 2024 to help prepare writers for a 2025 pitch event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If eligible, consider participating in mentoring to polish pitches; follow the event website/Twitter for mentoring application windows and pitch timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: #CheerPit — for authors with query-ready manuscripts and agented authors
rubrics_metrics.description: CheerPit is for writers with manuscripts at all stages; a specific announcement notes an event for authors with query-ready manuscripts as well as agented authors (date updated to Dec 9 in a comment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some CheerPit instances welcome agented authors as well as query-ready ones—read the announcement for any participant eligibility distinctions before posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple occurrences and repeat rules (events with several dates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some events (QuestPit, PitLight, PitDark, UnhingedPit, PBPitch historically) occur multiple times during the year; each date may have the same or slightly different rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat each listed date as a separate run—confirm which run you’re participating in and whether specifics (hashtags/platforms/targeted audiences) change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform migration & off-Twitter hosting
rubrics_metrics.description: Several events have moved off Twitter (PitBLK, LatinxPitch, PitchDis) or run on alternate platforms like Bluesky or Threads, or host pitches on private/password-protected sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because platforms differ in post length, media support, and moderation, check the host platform and adapt the pitch format accordingly; private sites may have submission windows and controlled access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event-specific targeting (unagented vs agented)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many events are explicitly for unagented authors (KidLitPit, PBPitch, SmallPitch, PitchDis, JoyPit) while others are open to all or include agented authors; some have separate tags for agent-targeted pitches (e.g., #PopUpPitA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only submit to events that match your agented status and goals; mis-targeting (posting an agented-pitch to an unagented-only event) may be against event rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre- or identity-specific entry requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Several events are targeted by genre or identity (PitDark for dark lit, PicantePit for Latinx/Latine adult/NA fiction, SEAsianPit, QueerPit, PitBLK), expecting self-identification or genre fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow any community guidance on self-identification and ensure your work aligns with the event’s focus; these events often center representation and community safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of themed hashtags and suffixes
rubrics_metrics.description: Events may require specific hashtags or suffixes (e.g., #PopUpPitA/#PopUpPitE, #LuckyPit, #LookingForBetas) to signal the purpose or audience of a pitch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurately tag your post so it reaches the intended audience (agents, editors, beta readers, critique partners). Mis-tagging can reduce visibility or violate event norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice forms and preparatory materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Some events (PitchDis) provide practice pitch forms ahead of the event so participants can familiarise themselves with the format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use available practice forms to test pitch length/format and to reduce posting errors during the live event; check dates when practice resources are published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community-building vs. industry-seeking events
rubrics_metrics.description: Some events are explicitly community-building/positivity events (PitLight, ChaosPit) while others explicitly aim to attract agent/editor attention (LatinxPitch website showcase, PitBLK private review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether your goal is industry exposure or community feedback and select events accordingly; tailor pitch tone and content to match the event’s purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staged submission and review windows for curated showcases
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain events separate submission and agent/editor-review windows (e.g., LatinxPitch submission dates followed by viewing dates; PitBLK’s submission/review timeline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare pitches to be viewed asynchronously—ensure clarity and polish since agents/editors may view posts days later rather than in an immediate feed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event status indicators (on hiatus/discontinued)
rubrics_metrics.description: The page lists discontinued/inactive events (e.g., #APIpit on hiatus, #PBPitch ended after June 2024, #PitMad ended in 2022, #DVpit indefinite hiatus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume listed events are active—check the status on the organiser’s channels; discontinued events may still influence history or community expectations but won’t be venues for pitching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event infrastructure beyond Twitter (Discord, private sites)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some events use additional infrastructure such as Discord communities (PicantePit), private pitch sites (PitBLK), or websites for showcases rather than live Twitter threads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate whether community discussion, mentoring, or pitch hosting occurs outside the social timeline and prepare any required files, images, or account access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting pitches for site showcases vs. social timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Website showcases and private pitch sites may display pitches differently than social timelines; some events encourage visual assets (moodboards) or require specific submission form fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft pitches to be clear in whichever medium the event uses—concise and eye-catching for timelines; slightly longer or structured for web showcases or forms that solicit metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentoring and preparatory programs tied to events
rubrics_metrics.description: Some events (SWANApit, SmoochPit historically mentioned as a mentoring contest) offer mentoring programs to prepare writers for pitch events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If mentoring is available and you are eligible, consider applying to improve your pitch and query materials ahead of the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience and goal alignment when choosing events
rubrics_metrics.description: Select events that align with your manuscript’s stage, genre, and representation identity—many events explicitly define who should participate (unagented, picture books, disabled writers, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choosing the right event increases the chance your pitch reaches sympathetic industry eyes or supportive community members—read event blurbs carefully.
